name: Getting data and cleaning it in Power Query

asg.t: Turn the messy export into a clean table
steps: Load RawOrdersExport with Get Data → Enter Data.
Remove the first row (report header) and the last row (TOTAL) using Remove Top Rows and Remove Bottom Rows, not by filtering on a value.
Trim and Clean every text column. Rename headers to PascalCase with no spaces.
Fix Order Dt: use Column From Examples or Locale-aware Change Type so all seven date formats become one Date column. Check every row.
Strip $ and " USD" from Unit Price and convert to Decimal Number. Replace "N/A" with null, then convert Qty to Whole Number.
Capitalize Each Word on customer name and Region, so "west " and "WEST" both become "West".
Remove exact duplicate rows. Delete the fully empty LegacyFlag column.
asg.exp: 27 rows, 8 columns, no errors, no text-typed numbers. Qty column shows 3 nulls (two "N/A" values and one blank). Exactly 4 distinct Region values.

asg.t: Reproduce the same clean-up as a reusable query
steps: Right-click your cleaned query → Reference. Name it "Orders Clean".
In the original query, disable Enable Load so only the referenced query lands in the model.
Change one input value in the Enter Data source (e.g. change $199.99 to $209.99) and refresh: the clean query must update without a single manual step.
asg.exp: Model contains one table, "Orders Clean". Query pane shows the raw query in italics (not loaded).

steps: In Orders Clean, Merge Queries with DimProduct on product name. Notice that "TRAIL CHEF STOVE" does not match: fix casing before the merge, not after.
Use Left Outer, then check the row count. Then try Inner and see which rows disappeared and why.
asg.exp: All 27 rows keep a Category after the casing fix. The Inner join initially loses 1 row before the fix.

steps: Turn on Column quality, Column distribution and Column profile in the View ribbon.
Change profiling from "top 1000 rows" to "entire data set".
Write down, for Qty: % valid, % error, % empty, distinct count, unique count.
asg.exp: You can explain the difference between distinct and unique out loud (distinct = different values, unique = values that occur exactly once).

int.q: What is the difference between Remove Duplicates and Remove Rows → Remove Errors, and when would each silently corrupt your data?
int.a: Remove Duplicates only checks the selected columns, so selecting one column drops rows that differ elsewhere. Remove Errors removes the entire row, so a single unparseable date deletes a real sale. Fix the type conversion (locale, Replace Values) so errors don't occur, and only remove errors as a last resort you can justify.

int.q: Why does Change Type to Date fail on "Jan 7 2026" and "06/02/2026" in the same column, and how do you fix it?
int.a: Type detection uses one culture. Use Change Type with Locale for a consistent format, or Column From Examples to build a parsing step. For truly mixed formats, split into a conditional column that tries Date.FromText with different cultures via try…otherwise.

int.q: Someone applied steps in the wrong order: Change Type before Replace Values. What breaks?
int.a: The type step errors on "$199.99" before replace runs. Steps are a pipeline; drag Replace Values above Change Type, or delete the auto-detected Changed Type step and re-add it at the end.

int.q: What is query folding and how can a beginner check whether a step folds?
int.a: Folding pushes the transformation back to the source as SQL. Right-click a step → View Native Query. If it is greyed out, folding stopped at or before that step. Enter Data never folds because there is no source engine.

int.q: When is a Reference better than a Duplicate?
int.a: Reference keeps a live link so the cleaning logic exists once. Duplicate copies the steps and they drift apart. Use Reference for staging → clean → model layers, Duplicate when you intentionally want two independent queries.

ass.q: After Remove Top Rows(1) and Remove Bottom Rows(1) on RawOrdersExport, how many rows remain before de-duplication?
ass.why: 30 total minus the header row and the TOTAL row = 28. Removing the one duplicate SO-5001 line gets you to 27.

ass.q: Which step turns "$699.99" into a usable number with the fewest chances of error?
ass.why: Replace then type-convert is explicit and survives future values like "$1,299.00" after you also replace commas.

ass.q: Load RawOrdersExport and produce a table with exactly these column types: OrderRef Text, OrderDate Date, CustomerName Text, Product Text, Qty Whole Number, UnitPrice Decimal, Region Text, Notes Text. Zero error cells. Screenshot the Applied Steps pane.
ass.hint: Order of steps: remove rows → replace values → trim/clean/capitalize → change type → remove duplicates.

ass.q: Column profile says Qty has distinct = 9 and unique = 3. What does unique = 3 mean?
o: 3 different values of Qty appear only once
ass.why: Unique counts values that occur exactly one time; distinct counts different values.
